headline: Write the plan first. It defines the design basis, the level of service, and every project that follows.
budget_note: Fixed-fee professional services. Issue A and Issue B proposed separately so the owner authorises the framework without committing to the final document before the scope of investigation is known.
regulatory_driver: NPDES MS4 · Miami-Dade Chapter 24 · SFWMD Environmental Resource Permit · Consent Order close-out
scope: Issue A — Framework and roadmap. Establish the design basis, the regulatory framework, and the adopted level of service the property will be held to for each design storm. | Define the stormwater system as currently understood, and state explicitly and in writing what is not known. | Define the investigation program required to close each gap, and set the sequence and dependencies between the projects that follow. | Establish the asset identification convention so every structure and pipe carries a permanent identifier from the first day of field work. | Define the performance criteria against which the finished system will be judged. | Issue B — Final governing plan. Incorporate the investigation, survey, geotechnical, modelling and design results as they arrive. | Consolidate the complete record set: drawings, calculations, permits, test data and certifications, into one governing document. | Document the implementation sequence actually executed and the as-built configuration of the system. | Publish and maintain the plan in ProjOS as the live reference for the stormwater system.
deliverables: Stormwater Management Plan — Issue A: framework, design basis, level of service, investigation roadmap | Project sequence and dependency map | Asset identification convention | Performance criteria | Stormwater Management Plan — Issue B: final governing document with the complete record set | Live plan published in ProjOS

headline: Determine what documentation of the stormwater system actually exists before spending a dollar in the field.
budget_note: Fixed-fee professional services. Agency records request and reproduction fees passed through at cost.
regulatory_driver: NPDES MS4 · Miami-Dade Chapter 24 · SFWMD Environmental Resource Permit history
scope: Search and retrieve records from the City of Opa-Locka, Miami-Dade DERM, Miami-Dade RER, the Water Control District, SFWMD and the building department. | Pursue original developer, architect and engineer files, plats, easements, drainage permits and prior modification permits. | Review historical aerials and Sanborn maps to identify the original drainage configuration and any later alterations. | Specifically pursue any record of the second retention area — its location, permitted volume and whether it was ever built. | Produce a records inventory and, more importantly, a gap register: what we have, what we do not have, and what each gap costs to close in the field.
deliverables: Records inventory with source and reliability rating on every document | Gap register mapped to the field projects required to close each gap | Recommendation memo: documentation-led path or field-led path | Findings written into the Stormwater Management Plan

project_name: CCTV Inspection of the Underground Stormwater System
headline: Send a camera through every pipe, catch basin to catch basin, and find out what is actually down there.
fee_basis: Subcontracted at cost plus 10% overhead and 10% profit; APAS administers
budget_note: Specialty subcontract procured and administered by APAS. Heavily obstructed or collapsed reaches requiring point excavation to access are handled as a separate authorised item.
regulatory_driver: NPDES MS4 illicit discharge detection · Miami-Dade Chapter 24 · Consent Order corrective actions
scope: Locate, open and inventory every drainage structure on the property; apply the permanent numbering convention set in the Stormwater Management Plan. | Clean and jet lines as required to obtain a usable inspection. | CCTV every reach, catch basin to catch basin, with continuous video and distance-referenced logging. | Record for every reach: pipe diameter, material, joint type, slope indication, and whether the pipe is perforated or solid. | Grade structural and operational condition to NASSCO PACP standard — cracking, deformation, offset joints, root intrusion, sediment depth, and full or partial collapse. | Flag illicit connections and any discharge that does not belong in a stormwater line. | Deliver a condition-ranked defect register that drives the repair and rehabilitation priority list. | Hand the pipe network geometry directly to the survey team so the survey is verifying a known network rather than discovering one.
deliverables: Complete structure and pipe inventory with permanent IDs | Full CCTV video library, indexed and reach-referenced | NASSCO PACP condition report with defect coding | Condition-ranked defect and rehabilitation priority register | Network geometry file issued to survey

headline: Produce a signed and sealed survey of the site surface and the drainage network, informed by what the camera found.
fee_basis: Subcontracted at cost plus 10% overhead and 10% profit; APAS administers
budget_note: Licensed survey subcontract procured and administered by APAS, including control establishment and NAVD 88 tie.
regulatory_driver: Miami-Dade Chapter 24 · SFWMD ERP submittal requirements · FEMA floodplain reference
scope: Topographic survey of the full site: finished floor elevations of every building, roadway and parking crowns and gutters, swales, curbs and site boundaries. | Locate and elevate every drainage structure identified in the CCTV inventory — rim and invert on every pipe entering and leaving. | Tie the survey to NAVD 88 and to the Miami-Dade County control network. | Reconcile the surveyed network against the CCTV inventory and resolve every discrepancy before sealing. | Deliver signed and sealed drawings plus editable CAD, and a survey-grade base map that becomes the single geometric basis for all subsequent stormwater design.
deliverables: Signed and sealed topographic and utility survey | Editable CAD (DWG/DXF) base map | Rim and invert schedule for every structure | Reconciliation memo against the CCTV inventory

headline: Measure how fast this soil actually absorbs water, so the hydraulic model is built on site data rather than assumption.
fee_basis: Subcontracted at cost plus 10% overhead and 10% profit; APAS administers
budget_note: Geotechnical subcontract procured and administered by APAS. Number of test locations set in the proposal; additional locations priced per unit.
regulatory_driver: Miami-Dade Chapter 24 exfiltration trench design criteria · SFWMD ERP
scope: Select boring and test locations using the survey and CCTV results, targeting proposed exfiltration and retention areas. | Advance soil borings with continuous sampling and classification. | Perform in-situ permeability testing using the Miami-Dade accepted method to establish the hydraulic conductivity value. | Establish the seasonal high water table elevation at each location. | Deliver a geotechnical report with design-ready parameters, signed and sealed.
deliverables: Signed and sealed geotechnical report | Hydraulic conductivity values by location | Seasonal high water table elevations | Design parameter summary issued to the modelling team

headline: Establish the pond's real shape, depth and current storage volume — above and below the waterline.
fee_basis: Subcontracted at cost plus 10% overhead and 10% profit; APAS administers
budget_note: Survey subcontract procured and administered by APAS, including boat or float-based bathymetric collection.
regulatory_driver: SFWMD ERP permitted storage volume · Miami-Dade Chapter 24
scope: Topographic survey of the pond banks, top of bank, side slopes and control structure. | Bathymetric survey of the pond bottom on a defined grid, capturing the sediment surface. | Probe to establish the depth of accumulated sediment and the original design bottom where recoverable. | Survey and document the outfall control structure, including weir elevations and orifice dimensions. | Compute the current stage-storage relationship and compare it against the permitted design storage.
deliverables: Pond topographic and bathymetric survey | Sediment thickness map | Current versus permitted stage-storage curve | Control structure documentation

project_name: Digital Terrain Model & Dredge Volume Determination
headline: Turn the pond survey into a three-dimensional model and compute exactly how much material has to come out.
budget_note: Fixed-fee professional services — analysis and drawing production from existing survey data.
regulatory_driver: SFWMD ERP storage restoration · construction quantity basis
scope: Build a digital terrain model of the existing sediment surface and of the target design bottom. | Compute cut volumes between the two surfaces, with contingency banding. | Produce dredge limit drawings and target elevation contours for the contractor. | Establish the measurement and verification method for confirming completion and final quantities. | Model the post-dredge stage-storage curve to confirm the storage volume recovered.
deliverables: Digital terrain model (existing and design surfaces) | Computed dredge volume with contingency band | Dredge limit and target elevation drawings | Measurement and verification protocol | Post-dredge stage-storage curve

headline: Sample and profile the sediment before it moves, so it goes to a facility that will legally accept it.
fee_basis: Lump sum professional services + subcontracted work at cost plus 10% overhead and 10% profit
budget_note: APAS professional services on a fixed fee; laboratory, hauling and disposal procured and administered by APAS. Disposal cost is governed by the characterization result — which is precisely why it is determined early and cheaply.
regulatory_driver: Miami-Dade DERM · FDEP solid waste rules · Chapter 62-701 F.A.C.
scope: Develop a sampling and analysis plan appropriate to the pond and the surrounding land uses. | Collect representative sediment samples across the pond footprint and at depth. | Laboratory analysis for the contaminants of concern indicated by the adjacent land uses, including metals and petroleum constituents. | Prepare the waste profile and obtain written acceptance from the receiving facility before dredging begins. | Determine the disposal pathway and confirm hauling, manifesting and chain of custody requirements. | Manage transport and disposal during dredging, with full manifest documentation retained for the compliance record.
deliverables: Sampling and analysis plan | Laboratory analytical results | Approved waste profile and written facility acceptance | Disposal pathway determination memo | Complete manifest and chain of custody file

headline: Remove the accumulated sediment and restore the pond to its design storage volume.
fee_basis: Subcontracted at cost plus 10% overhead and 10% profit; APAS administers
budget_note: Construction subcontract procured and administered by APAS against the measured quantity from STM-07. Disposal handled under STM-08.
regulatory_driver: SFWMD ERP · Miami-Dade DERM dewatering and turbidity permits · Consent Order
scope: Procure and contract the dredging work against the computed volume and dredge limit drawings. | Mobilise, install turbidity and erosion controls, and establish the dewatering and staging area. | Dredge to the design bottom elevation within the defined limits. | Dewater the removed material to a transportable moisture content. | Restore banks and side slopes; stabilise and re-vegetate disturbed areas, including the littoral zone. | Post-dredge verification survey confirming target elevations and the storage volume recovered.
deliverables: Executed dredging contract against measured quantities | Turbidity monitoring records | Post-dredge verification survey | Storage volume recovery certification | Bank restoration and stabilisation completion

headline: Model the whole property against the 5-year, 25-year and 100-year storms and find out where the water goes.
budget_note: Fixed-fee professional services — model build, calibration, three-storm analysis and scenario testing.
regulatory_driver: Miami-Dade Chapter 24 · SFWMD ERP · FEMA · NPDES MS4 · Consent Order
scope: Build the model from the survey base map, the CCTV network geometry, the geotechnical permeability values and the pond stage-storage curve. | Calibrate against observed flooding history on the property where records or resident reports exist. | Run the 5-year, 25-year and 100-year design storms for the applicable durations. | Evaluate two protection criteria explicitly and separately: finished floor elevation protection for every building, and roadway passability for emergency access. | Identify every deficiency — undersized pipes, insufficient storage, inadequate pumping, low points and overland flow paths. | Test improvement scenarios and quantify the flood-risk reduction each one buys. | Determine whether the pond and pipe network alone can meet the required level of service, or whether supplemental features are needed. | Write the results into the Stormwater Management Plan as the governing design basis.
deliverables: Calibrated hydrologic and hydraulic model | Flood maps and inundation depths for each return period | Finished floor and roadway risk assessment by building and by street | Deficiency register with hydraulic cause identified | Improvement scenario comparison with risk reduction quantified | Determination on the need for supplemental features

project_name: Stormwater Lift Station — Adequacy Assessment, Siting & Design
headline: Determine whether the pumping capacity serving the pond is adequate, whether it is in the right place, and design what it should be.
budget_note: Fixed-fee professional services — assessment, siting and design. Construction proposed separately once the design is set.
regulatory_driver: SFWMD ERP · Miami-Dade Chapter 24 · flood protection level of service
scope: Assess the existing lift station: condition, capacity, controls, power supply and reliability. | Evaluate its location relative to the retention pond and to the modelled inflow points. | Determine required firm capacity against the modelled design storms. | Evaluate siting alternatives where relocation is indicated. | Produce design drawings and specifications for the selected configuration, including wet well, pumps, controls, standby power and telemetry. | Establish the permitting pathway and prepare permit-ready documents.
deliverables: Adequacy and condition assessment report | Siting alternatives evaluation with recommendation | Signed and sealed design drawings and specifications | Permit-ready submittal package

headline: Design the pond to the storage volume the model requires, not the volume it happens to have.
budget_note: Fixed-fee professional services — design and permitting. Construction proposed separately once quantities are set.
regulatory_driver: SFWMD ERP · Miami-Dade Chapter 24 allowable discharge rate
scope: Design the pond to the target storage volume and stage-storage relationship established by the hydraulic model. | Design side slopes, safety shelf, littoral zone and maintenance access. | Design the outfall control structure — weir, orifice and discharge rate — to the permitted allowable discharge. | Integrate with the lift station design and confirm combined performance. | Prepare permit-ready drawings, calculations and specifications.
deliverables: Signed and sealed pond design drawings | Stage-storage-discharge calculations | Control structure design | Permit submittal package

project_name: Site Regrading & Recontouring — Design, Permit & Construct
headline: Reshape the ground so that water goes where the model says it should go.
fee_basis: Lump sum professional services + subcontracted work at cost plus 10% overhead and 10% profit
budget_note: Design and permitting on a fixed fee; construction procured and administered by APAS. Scope is entirely determined by the model, so the construction proposal follows STM-10.
parties: APAS · Engineer of Record · General contractor
regulatory_driver: Miami-Dade Chapter 24 · SFWMD ERP · City of Opa-Locka · Consent Order · FEMA
scope: Design regrading and recontouring to achieve the drainage patterns and hydraulic capacity established by the model. | Set finished floor protection and roadway crown elevations to the adopted level of service. | Design conveyance improvements — swales, inlets, pipe upsizing — where the model identifies capacity deficiency. | Permit through Miami-Dade DERM, SFWMD and the City of Opa-Locka. | Phase construction to maintain resident access, parking and emergency vehicle circulation throughout. | Construct, with survey verification of finished grades against design. | Restore paving, landscaping and site features.
deliverables: Signed and sealed grading and drainage drawings | Approved permits | Phased construction plan with resident access maintained | Constructed improvements with as-built survey verification | Record drawings issued into the Stormwater Management Plan

project_name: Supplemental Stormwater Features — Exfiltration Trench & the Second Retention Area
headline: If the model says the pond and pipes are not enough, add capacity — and finally settle the question of the second retention area.
fee_basis: Lump sum professional services + subcontracted work at cost plus 10% overhead and 10% profit
budget_note: Conditional — proposed only if the model identifies a residual storage deficit. Investigation and design on a fixed fee; construction procured and administered by APAS.
regulatory_driver: Miami-Dade Chapter 24 exfiltration criteria · SFWMD ERP
scope: Locate and confirm the second retention area through records, historical aerials, geophysical survey and field investigation. | If found: assess its condition, permitted status and residual storage capacity, and determine whether restoration is viable and cost-effective. | If not found: document the investigation and formally close the question so it stops appearing as an open assumption in every future analysis. | Design an exfiltration trench system sized to the residual storage deficit, using the measured hydraulic conductivity from the geotechnical work. | Compare the two options on capacity delivered, cost, permitability and long-term maintenance burden. | Permit and construct the selected option.
deliverables: Second retention area investigation report — located and assessed, or formally closed out | Exfiltration trench design and calculations | Options comparison with recommendation | Permits and constructed improvements

headline: Turn the plan into a running operation — the same way the sewer extension was operationalized.
budget_note: Fixed-fee professional services — plan development, ProjOS configuration and staff handover.
regulatory_driver: NPDES MS4 operations and maintenance · Consent Order · Miami-Dade Chapter 24
scope: Define routine inspection and maintenance procedures for every asset class — catch basins, pipes, pond, control structure, lift station and any supplemental features. | Set inspection frequencies, cleaning cycles and sediment removal triggers, so storage loss is caught early rather than rediscovered in a decade. | Establish pre-storm readiness and post-storm response procedures. | Define the regulatory reporting calendar and the responsible party for each submittal. | Establish record-keeping, evidence retention and the annual system condition review. | Define performance monitoring, alarm thresholds and escalation paths. | Build the operating record into ProjOS with scheduled tasks, evidence capture and automatic compliance reporting.
deliverables: Stormwater Operations Plan | Inspection and maintenance schedule by asset class | Pre-storm and post-storm response procedures | Regulatory reporting calendar with named responsibility | ProjOS operating record with scheduled tasks and evidence capture | Staff training and handover

project_name: Conveyance & Close-Out to the City of Opa-Locka
headline: Transfer the completed sewer extension to the City so it becomes the City's asset to own, operate and maintain.
budget_note: Fixed-fee professional services for coordination and package assembly. Excludes the Utilities Performance Security, the final-obligations cash bond, and City review fees, all of which sit with the owner.
parties: APAS (lead) · Engineer of Record · Surveyor · Contractors · Owner's counsel
regulatory_driver: City of Opa-Locka Utilities Conveyance Checklist · Miami-Dade DERM · FDEP General Permit · Prime Contract PC-01
scope: Run the City of Opa-Locka Utilities Conveyance Checklist to completion, item by item, with a named owner and a date against every line. | Coordinate the Engineer of Record deliverables: signed and sealed record drawings, infiltration and exfiltration certification, Engineer's Final Payment Confirmation, FDEP sewer certification, General Permit and In-Service Letter, latitude and longitude detail sheet, and the record-drawing disk. | Coordinate the surveyor's signed and sealed as-built survey (PDF plus editable CAD) and reconcile it against the record drawings. | Coordinate the contractor's CCTV video of the constructed gravity sewer, the Sewer Report and the Master Utility Sheet, plus field completion and restoration for the City's preliminary inspection. | Close the contractor package: punch list completion, final lien waivers, material certifications, test results, permit close-outs, and asphalt and sod final quantities. | Execute and file the three twelve-month warranties by building group — Building 3 South with Building 4; Building 5 with Building 6; and Building 3 North. | Support owner's counsel on the legal and security items: Attorney's and Owner's Affidavits, Warranty Deed and Bill of Sale, UCC subordination, and the Utilities Performance Security. | Assemble, transmit and track the acceptance package through City review to written acceptance.
deliverables: Completed Utilities Conveyance Checklist with evidence attached to every line | Transmittal package to the City of Opa-Locka | Executed warranty set (three building groups) | Written City acceptance and asset transfer confirmation | Retainage release documentation per the contract schedule

project_name: Master Effluent Flow Meter at the Property Discharge Point
headline: Install a permanent flow meter where wastewater leaves the property, so total discharge to the City pump station is a measured fact.
fee_basis: Lump sum professional services + subcontracted work at cost plus 10% overhead and 10% profit
budget_note: Design, permitting and commissioning on a fixed fee; structure, meter, telemetry and installation procured and administered by APAS.
parties: APAS · Engineer of Record · Contractor · City of Opa-Locka
regulatory_driver: City of Opa-Locka wastewater discharge accounting · DERM · FDEP · I&I reduction
scope: Confirm the single point of discharge from the property to the City's collection system and verify there is no secondary or bypass connection. | Design a permanent metering structure — vault or dedicated manhole — sized and located for safe, permanent access and for accurate hydraulic conditions. | Select and specify the metering technology appropriate to the flow regime, with redundancy on the primary reading. | Design telemetry and continuous data logging so the record is automatic, timestamped and retrievable, not a monthly clipboard reading. | Permit through the City of Opa-Locka and Miami-Dade DERM as required. | Construct, commission and field-calibrate; establish the certified accuracy baseline. | Run a baseline infiltration and inflow study using the new meter — diurnal flow curves and wet-weather response — to quantify how much of what we discharge is groundwater and rainwater rather than sanitary flow. | Integrate the meter data feed into ProjOS for continuous monitoring and exception alerting.
deliverables: Signed and sealed design drawings and specifications | Approved permits | Constructed and commissioned metering station | Calibration certificate and accuracy baseline | Baseline I&I report with wet-weather response curves | Live data feed into ProjOS

project_name: Water & Sewer Records and File Assessment
headline: Review every available file to establish what is documented about the water and sewer systems on this property.
budget_note: Lump sum, scope approved. Covers the expanded all-utilities review. Agency records request and reproduction fees passed through at cost.
regulatory_driver: Miami-Dade WASD · Chapter 24 · City of Opa-Locka utility records
scope: Search and retrieve from the City of Opa-Locka, Miami-Dade Water and Sewer Department, DERM, RER and the building department. | Pursue original developer, architect and engineer record sets, plats, easements and utility agreements. | Retrieve permit history: water main extensions, service connections, meter installations and backflow device records. | Review historical aerials and prior construction documents for evidence of utility modifications over time. | Assess each document for reliability — sealed as-built, permit set, sketch or hearsay — and rate it accordingly. | Produce a records inventory and a gap register identifying exactly what remains unknown.
deliverables: Records inventory with source and reliability rating | Gap register: what is documented and what is not | Recommendation memo on the field verification path

project_name: Water Distribution Field Verification & As-Built Development
headline: Establish where the water pipes actually are — from the records if they hold up, from the field if they do not.
fee_basis: Lump sum professional services + subcontracted work at cost plus 10% overhead and 10% profit
budget_note: Proposed against whichever path the file assessment establishes. APAS professional services on a fixed fee; survey and locating procured and administered by APAS.
parties: APAS · Surveyor · Subsurface utility locating contractor
regulatory_driver: Miami-Dade Chapter 24 · WASD standards · Sunshine 811 · construction risk mitigation
scope: Path A — records adequate: field-verify at control points, reconcile against the documentation, and produce an as-built from the record set. | Path B — records inadequate: full field verification survey using electromagnetic pipe locating and ground-penetrating radar across the site. | Survey and elevate all surface appurtenances: valves, hydrants, meters, backflow devices and service points. | Pothole at critical locations and at points of future work to confirm horizontal position, depth, diameter and material. | Reconcile all field data against whatever records exist and resolve every conflict. | Produce a signed and sealed water system as-built in PDF and editable CAD. | Identify unknown, abandoned or unmapped lines and flag them for follow-up.
deliverables: Signed and sealed water distribution as-built | Editable CAD (DWG/DXF) | Valve, hydrant, meter and appurtenance schedule | Potholing records with depth, diameter and material confirmed | Register of unknown or abandoned lines

project_name: Water Meter Box Program — Design, Permit & Construct
headline: Design, permit and build the meter boxes; the City of Opa-Locka installs its meters into them.
fee_basis: Lump sum professional services + subcontracted work at cost plus 10% overhead and 10% profit
budget_note: Design and permitting on a fixed fee; construction procured and administered by APAS against the meter count established in WTR-02. Excludes City meters and City fees.

regulatory_driver: City of Opa-Locka · Miami-Dade WASD standards · Chapter 24
scope: Determine meter count, sizing and locations from the as-built and from the service configuration. | Design meter box installations to City of Opa-Locka and Miami-Dade WASD standards, including box, setting, service piping and appurtenances. | Locate boxes for permanent access, safe reading and protection from vehicle traffic. | Permit through the City of Opa-Locka and WASD. | Construct with resident water service maintained; phase and notice all interruptions. | Coordinate City meter installation: schedule, inspect, witness and document. | Verify and document every installation, and record final meter numbers against service addresses.
deliverables: Meter schedule with sizing and locations | Signed and sealed design drawings | Approved permits | Constructed and inspected meter boxes | City meter installation coordination and completion record | Meter number to service address register

project_name: Backflow Prevention Program — Design, Permit & Install
headline: Install backflow prevention at every required connection and enrol the devices in certified annual testing.
fee_basis: Lump sum professional services + subcontracted work at cost plus 10% overhead and 10% profit
budget_note: Design and permitting on a fixed fee; devices, installation and initial certification procured and administered by APAS. Annual testing thereafter carried under ongoing compliance services.
parties: APAS · Engineer of Record · Contractor · Certified backflow tester
regulatory_driver: Miami-Dade Chapter 24 cross-connection control · City of Opa-Locka · F.A.C. 62-555 · Safe Drinking Water Act
scope: Survey all connections and determine the required device type and hazard classification at each. | Design installations to City of Opa-Locka and WASD standards, with permanent access and traffic protection. | Permit through the City and WASD. | Procure, install, and commission all devices. | Perform initial certification testing by a certified tester and file the results with the City. | Enrol every device in the annual testing and certification program, with the schedule and evidence capture built into ProjOS. | Build the device register: location, type, serial number, installation date and test history.
deliverables: Cross-connection hazard survey and device schedule | Signed and sealed design drawings and permits | Installed and commissioned devices | Initial certification test reports filed with the City | Device register with full test history in ProjOS | Annual testing program with scheduled reminders

headline: Put in an irrigation well to serve the common areas, and take that demand off the potable system.
fee_basis: Lump sum professional services + subcontracted work at cost plus 10% overhead and 10% profit
budget_note: Siting, permitting and construction management on a fixed fee; drilling, pump, controls and distribution procured and administered by APAS.
regulatory_driver: Miami-Dade DERM well permit · SFWMD water use permit · Chapter 24 cross-connection control
scope: Hydrogeologic siting: aquifer selection, expected yield, water quality and required setbacks from sanitary and environmental features. | Coordinate siting explicitly with the environmental monitoring well program so the two do not conflict. | Permit through Miami-Dade DERM and SFWMD, including water use authorisation. | Drill, develop and test the well; confirm yield and water quality. | Install pump, controls, and above-ground equipment with backflow protection. | Design and construct the irrigation distribution to the common areas, with zoning and controller. | Commission, test and hand over with an operations and maintenance manual.
deliverables: Hydrogeologic siting report | DERM and SFWMD permits | Completed well with yield and water quality test results | Pump, controls and distribution system installed and commissioned | Operations and maintenance manual | Potable demand reduction baseline

headline: Find out how much of the water this property buys never reaches a bill — and how much of that is recoverable.
authorization: For discussion before anything is scoped
budget_note: Not yet scoped. APAS would like to discuss the objective and the audit period with the owner before proposing anything. A preliminary balance can be built from existing billing records; resolution improves substantially once WTR-03 metering is in and WTR-05 has taken irrigation off the potable system.
regulatory_driver: Owner operating cost · AWWA M36 · City of Opa-Locka billing reconciliation · water conservation
scope: Establish the system input volume from the City's master metering and billing history, and verify the accuracy of the meter producing that number. | Assemble billed consumption from the meter records and reconcile it against the input volume over a defined audit period. | Build the water balance to the AWWA M36 standard, separating unbilled authorized consumption from apparent losses and real losses. | Quantify apparent losses: meter under-registration by age and size, data handling and billing gaps, and any unauthorized or unrecorded connections. | Quantify real losses and compute the Infrastructure Leakage Index, so the result can be compared against the technical minimum for a system of this size rather than against a generic benchmark. | Run a minimum night flow analysis using continuous logging, since night-time residual flow is the most direct available indicator of leakage. | Evaluate whether dividing the site into district metered areas would be worthwhile, so future losses can be localised to a block rather than to the property as a whole. | Quantify the annual dollar value of the loss at the City's current rate, and rank the recovery measures by cost against recoverable volume. | Establish an ongoing tracking method in ProjOS so the figure is monitored continuously rather than rediscovered every few years.
deliverables: AWWA M36 water balance for the audit period | Non-revenue water volume and percentage, with the dollar value at current rates | Apparent versus real loss split with the basis for each | Infrastructure Leakage Index | Minimum night flow analysis | Ranked loss-recovery recommendations with cost against recoverable volume | Ongoing non-revenue water tracking in ProjOS

project_name: Adjacent Property Environmental File Review & Plume Assessment
headline: Review the environmental history of every property surrounding this one — the junkyards above all — and determine where contamination could be coming from.
budget_note: Fixed-fee professional services. Agency file review fees and database search costs passed through at cost.
regulatory_driver: Miami-Dade DERM Chapter 24 · FDEP Chapter 62-780 F.A.C. · owner due diligence
scope: Identify every adjacent and nearby property on all four sides and establish its current and historical use. | Focus the review on the junkyard and salvage operations, which are the most probable sources. | Search the regulatory databases: DERM, FDEP and EPA records — RCRA, CERCLIS, petroleum storage, dry cleaning and industrial waste files. | Retrieve and review enforcement history, contamination assessment reports and remediation records for each source property. | Review historical aerials, Sanborn maps and city directories to reconstruct site use over time. | Establish the contaminants of concern based on documented use and documented releases. | Determine the groundwater gradient and flow direction across the property from regional and site data. | Model probable plume vectors: which boundaries are downgradient of which sources, and where migration onto Glorieta Gardens would first appear.
deliverables: Adjacent property environmental history report | Contaminants of concern list with the documented basis for each | Groundwater flow direction and gradient determination | Plume vector analysis with probable migration pathways | Monitoring well siting recommendation and analytical parameter list

project_name: Boundary Monitoring Well Network — Design & Installation
headline: Install a monitoring well network on the property boundaries, positioned by the plume analysis.
fee_basis: Subcontracted at cost plus 10% overhead and 10% profit; APAS administers
budget_note: Drilling and installation subcontract procured and administered by APAS. Well count and depth set by the plume analysis and confirmed in the proposal.
parties: APAS · Environmental consultant · Licensed well contractor
regulatory_driver: Miami-Dade DERM Chapter 24 monitoring well permit · FDEP Chapter 62-780 F.A.C.
scope: Finalise well count, locations and screen intervals from the plume vector analysis, with upgradient wells for background and downgradient wells for detection. | Design each well to DERM standards: construction, screen interval, filter pack, seal and surface completion. | Locate wells for permanent access and protection from vehicles and site operations. | Coordinate placement with the irrigation well siting so the two programs do not interfere. | Permit through Miami-Dade DERM. | Drill, install, develop and survey each well; establish measuring point elevations to NAVD 88. | Conduct the initial round of groundwater elevation measurements and confirm the actual flow direction against the predicted gradient. | Build the well network register into ProjOS with location, construction detail and sampling history.
deliverables: Monitoring well network design and siting plan | DERM well permits | Installed, developed and surveyed wells with completion logs | Measuring point elevations tied to NAVD 88 | Confirmed groundwater flow direction from measured elevations | Well network register in ProjOS

headline: Sample the wells on a defined schedule and determine whether contamination is migrating onto the property.
fee_basis: Lump sum professional services + subcontracted work at cost plus 10% overhead and 10% profit
